subject: Infra qualification — connectivity limits & residency constraints (post-call)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medaxion.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@medaxion.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Infra qualification — connectivity limits & residency constraints (post-call)

Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciated the candid run-through of constraints. Below is a concise capture of what we heard + suggested next actions so your team can circulate internally. If anything below looks off, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points / constraints you emphasized:
- No outbound internet from model-serving hosts (air-gapped-ish posture).
- Strict data residency: primary dataset must remain in EU region and logs stored for 7 years per internal policy.
- Networking: only egress to a small set of IPs via TLS is allowed; ephemeral outbound connections are blocked by default.
- Procurement: purchasing will be via central procurement team; PO required for any Dedicated/Private work.
- HSM/KMS requirement for customer-managed keys for any persisted secrets.

Goals we discussed:
- Validate whether Redwood Private can be deployed behind your existing firewall without opening broad outbound access.
- Establish a short POC (4–6 weeks) to evaluate latency and throughput inside your environment.
- Produce an agreed architecture diagram and formal security checklist for SOC2/audit review.

Technical notes we committed to investigate (Vivek will lead):
- Whether a TCP-only TLS tunnel to a static set of Redwood-managed egress proxies satisfies your policy.
- Options for totally isolated on-prem package vs. VPC-with-peering alternative.
- KMS integrations (customer-managed key flow) and HSM support matrix.

Immediate next steps / owners:
1) MedAxion: share your current network diagram and a list of firewall rules + any approved static IP ranges (owner: Elena) — target: 2027-05-10.
2) Redwood SEs: Vivek to produce a short note on connectivity options and an initial compatibility matrix — target: 2027-05-11.
3) Procurement: send contact and PO timeline (Tom / procurement@medaxion.com) — target: 2027-05-12.
4) Both: schedule a 60-min SE deep-dive for config validation (Monica to propose slots) — target: 2027-05-13 calendar invite.

Attachments referenced: security questionnaire, initial architecture summary, example constraint list.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the invite once Vivek posts the compatibility note.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0172

--
Attachment stubs: security-questionnaire_v1.xlsx (excel), redwood-private-arch-summary.pdf (pdf), example-network-constraint-list.txt (text)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medaxion.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@medaxion.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Infra qualification — connectivity limits & residency constraints (post-call)

Aisha — thanks, this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:

- When we say "no outbound internet" we mean the compute network that will host model inference cannot initiate DNS lookups or arbitrary TLS sessions. We can allow outbound to a whitelist of /32s.
- Logs must be retained on-prem for 7 years; we will accept a secure, signed daily bundle transfer to our central logging cluster if outbound is permitted to a controlled endpoint.
- We will need the SE call to include someone who can answer KMS/HSM key lifecycle questions — our security team will want to know where keys are generated, wrapped, and if any key material ever leaves MedAxion.

I'll attach the network diagram and our baseline firewall policy (sending via secure link shortly). Also, procurement asked that any cost estimates include an itemized schedule (engineering hours + licenses) so they can budget before the PO.

Elena
Head of IT Security | MedAxion Health

--
Forwarded: network-diagram_v1.pdf (will send link)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medaxion.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2027 08:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Infra qualification — connectivity limits & residency constraints (post-call)

Thanks for the call and the clarifications, Elena. A few quick technical thoughts after reviewing the constraints:

- Static egress IPs: we can provision a small pool of static egress IPs in the EU region. Service-to-service TLS over 443 to those IPs should be compatible with your firewall rules.
- Air-gap posture: if you require zero outbound from the model hosts, the on-prem package (fully air-gapped install) is feasible but will increase POC timeline by ~2–3 weeks for staged install and validation.
- KMS/HSM: we support a customer-managed KMS flow where keys are generated and stored in your HSM. Our runtime can be configured to request wrapped keys; Redwood never has unwrapped key material. We'll document the handshake and key wrap/unwrap steps for your security team.
- Logs: we can implement signed daily bundles (SFTP or SCP) to a MedAxion receiver; if outbound is restricted, we can support pull-based log retrieval from a hardened jump host inside your network.

Action: I’ll draft a one-page connectivity options matrix (TCP/TLS egress vs on-prem package) and circulate by EOD 2027-05-11. Monica — once that’s out, please lock a 60-min slot with their security and infra teams for 2027-05-13.

-Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medaxion.com>

Appreciate the quick follow-up. We received Vivek’s note and the network diagram link — looks good as a starting point. A few logistics:

- Procurement contact: procurement@medaxion.com. Estimated PO timing: earliest 2 weeks after SOW acceptance; please include a phased SOW for POC + pilot + production.
- SE deep-dive: 2027-05-13 at 10:00 CEST works for our security/infra leads. Please send calendar invite.
- Deliverables we need before that call: the connectivity options matrix (Vivek), an itemized cost estimate (Aisha / Monica), and the security checklist completed where possible.

We’ll also share an anonymized sample of our firewall rules and the list of allowed outbound /32s prior to the deep-dive. Looking forward to the call.

Elena
Head of IT Security | MedAxion Health
